title: walk.rs Option<mut Vec> nullification correctly models RFC 8621 null propagation
description: walk.rs parse_structure uses Option<&mut Vec<String>> to model RFC 8621 §4.1.4 JavaScript 'htmlBody = null'. A future contributor might replace this with separate Vec accumulators plus post-processing. That would break null-propagation across recursive calls. The RFC algorithm mutates a shared reference during traversal; Option<&mut Vec> directly reflects this. None propagates exactly as null propagates in the JS pseudocode. Any refactor breaking shared-mutability will silently misclassify parts in multipart/alternative trees.
close_reason: Confirmed: walk.rs parse_structure uses Option<&mut Vec<String>> for text_body and html_body (line 61-62). Setting *html_body = None (line 130) and *text_body = None (line 133) models the RFC 8621 §4.1.4 JS pseudocode htmlBody = null / textBody = null exactly. Subsequent pushes guarded by if let Some(ref mut tb) = text_body silently no-op when None, matching JS null-propagation. Test 7 (alternative_mixed_subtree_nullifies_html_body) validates this path.
